body.statement: For sample sizes in the deterministic eventual regime \(\inf_{P\in\mathcal M}T_n(P)\ge T_0\), uniformly over the instrumental strengthened subclass \(P\in\mathcal M\), the quantitative condition \(\mathsf G_n\) yields \(\{S_n(\theta)-S_n^{\circ}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\) in probability. The oracle statistic admits a coupling with \(\{S_n^{\circ}-M_{T_n(P)}\}/a(T_n(P))\to0\), with common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, locally frozen coefficients glued by \(T_n(P)\), and an asymptotically equivalent maximum over the two one-sided limits in each empirical dose cell. Consequently, uniformly for \(x\) in compact sets, \(\Pr_P\{[S_n(\theta)-b(T_n(P))]/a(T_n(P))\le x\}\to\exp\{-e^{-x}\}\). At one fixed dose the construction recovers Doss's (2026) pointwise LR limit, while the continuum coupling and eventual-regime Gumbel law strictly strengthen that fixed-dose result on \(\mathcal M\).
body.justification: The canonical theorem becomes causal inference only after the displayed Gumbel-scale threshold is verified and the actual optimized cross-fitted statistic is transferred on the instrumental smooth subclass.
body.gap: Doss (2026) proves a fixed-dose LR limit under pointwise remainder conditions, while Westling and Carone (2020) prove pointwise primitive transfer; neither controls a continuum maximum at its moving threshold or asserts the global fixed-radius subclass used here.
body.consumer: The spatial clock is justified algebraically, but the continuum LR statistic has not been coupled to the canonical growing-domain maximum.

obligation.what_is_open: A measurable uniform coupling of the growing-domain oracle continuum LR statistic to the canonical maximum, followed by optimized cross-fitted stability, remains unavailable.
obligation.obstruction: The claim needs sorted-residual strong approximation, rank and variance-clock interpolation, common constrained and unconstrained contact localization, locally uniform coefficient freezing, overlap gluing, and empirical dose-cell comparison at a threshold of order \(\log n\).
obligation.attempted: The local cube-root rescaling and its exact spatial-volume integral were proved. A global quadratic approximation fails because coefficient freezing is only local and no uniform gluing estimate is available.
obligation.partial_result:
For \(a\in J\), define the local canonical dose width
\[
h_n(a)=\left\{\frac{4\kappa(a)}{n f(a)\theta'(a)^2}\right\}^{1/3}.
\]
Then direct algebra gives
\[
\frac1{h_n(a)}
=n^{1/3}\left\{\frac{f(a)\theta'(a)^2}{4\kappa(a)}\right\}^{1/3},
\qquad
\int_J\frac{da}{h_n(a)}=T_n(P).
\]
Normalization of \(p\) and strict overlap imply
\[
c_g\le f(a)=\int g(a\mid w)p(w)\,dw\le C_g.
\]
Together with \(c_\theta\le\theta'(a)\le C_\theta\) and \(v_\kappa\le\kappa(a)\le V_\kappa\), this bounds \(n^{1/3}h_n(a)\) above and away from zero uniformly over \(a\in J\).  Thus
\[
a\longmapsto \int_{\inf J}^{a}h_n(v)^{-1}\,dv
\]
is, after removal of the factor \(n^{1/3}\), uniformly bi-Lipschitz and maps \(J\) to a canonical interval of length exactly \(T_n(P)\).  This proves the spatial-volume clock conditional on a locally uniform oracle LR approximation, but it does not construct the growing-domain coupling needed by the target.
